To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chondrocytic cells can express desmin and alpha-SM-actin, which is an indication that the chondroid cells can transform into myochondroblastic and myochondroclastic cells.
the immunophenotypes of the chondrocytic cells in the cartilage defects are different from the phenotypes of the chontrocytes in intact cartilage.

the expression of desmin in chondrocyte cells is probably an indication of a healing process, and that desmin-positive chonrocytes are present in the repair tissue in human defective artifular cartilage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of muscle markers in human cartilage cells and the role of myochondroblastic and myochondroblasic transformation in the healing of the defects of articular cartilage.
a possible role of myochondroblastic/myochondrocytic cells during the repair processes of the articular surface.
the expression of desmin in the cartilage cells of human articular cartilage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the immunophenotypic expression of cartilage cells is very complex and it is not possible to draw a definite conclusion on their origin and differentiation on the basis of the immunophistochemical staining only.
the expression of smooth muscle actin in chondrocyte cells is not a constant finding and is probably a transient feature during the healing process of cartilage defects.
the expression of desmin and actin in chondrocyte is a sign of the transformation of the cartilage into the fibrocartilage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunostaining of cartilage cells for desmin and alpha-smooth actin could be used as a marker of cartilage repair.
the immunohistochemistry for desmin and alpha-smooth actin could be used as a marker for the detection of the cartilage repair process.
the chondrocyte phenotype is not a constant feature, but it is a variable and changeable characteristic of the cartilage cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chondrocyte immunophenotype is quite variable and it can be influenced by the environment of the cells.
desmin-positive cells in the human cartilage can be regarded as an expression of a myofibroblast phenotype.
the immunohistochemical examination of the articular chondrocyte phenotype is very useful in the diagnosis of cartilage defects.
